natural: Criss-crossed and tangled together

meaning.en: Intricate and complicated; tangled, with many interwoven parts.
meaning.zh: 形容头绪多，情况复杂。

examples.zh: 这起案件的关系错综复杂，警方调查了半年。
examples.en: The relationships in this case were so tangled that the police spent six months investigating.

examples.zh: 老城区的小巷错综复杂，很容易迷路。
examples.en: The lanes of the old town form a maze — it's easy to get lost.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. Used of relationships, situations, road networks, plots.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。用于关系、局势、道路、情节等。

natural: Shown one corner, work out the other three

meaning.en: To infer many things from one example; to learn by analogy.
meaning.zh: 比喻从一件事情类推而知道其他许多事情。

examples.zh: 学数学不能只背答案，要学会举一反三。
examples.en: In maths you can't just memorise answers — you have to learn to apply the method to new problems.

examples.zh: 老师讲了一个例子，他就能举一反三。
examples.en: After the teacher gives one example, he can work out the rest himself.

story.en: Confucius said: "If I hold up one corner and a student cannot come back with the other three, I do not repeat the lesson" (举一隅不以三隅反，则不复也). He expected students to reason from one example to others.
story.zh: 孔子说："举一隅不以三隅反，则不复也。"意思是教给学生一个方面，如果他不能由此推知其他三个方面，就不再教他了。

usage.en: Predicate. Especially common in education and study advice.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，尤其常用于学习、教育语境。

natural: Following the order and advancing step by step

meaning.en: To proceed step by step in the proper order; gradual, systematic progress.
meaning.zh: 按照一定的步骤逐渐深入或提高。

equivalents: Rome wasn't built in a day

examples.zh: 健身要循序渐进，一开始不要练得太猛。
examples.en: Build up your training gradually — don't overdo it at the start.

examples.zh: 这本教材内容循序渐进，适合自学。
examples.en: This textbook progresses step by step, so it's good for self-study.

story.en: Zhu Xi advised readers to study "in order and advance gradually" (循序而渐进), finishing one book before starting the next rather than skimming many at once.
story.zh: 朱熹在谈读书方法时主张"循序而渐进"，读完一本再读下一本，不要贪多求快。

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial. Common in study, training and policy contexts. Opposite of rushing (急于求成).
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语，常用于学习、训练、改革等。与"急于求成"相对。

natural: Understood in every family, known in every household

meaning.en: Known to everyone; a household name.
meaning.zh: 家家户户都知道。形容人人皆知。

examples.zh: 《西游记》在中国是家喻户晓的故事。
examples.en: Journey to the West is a story every household in China knows.

examples.zh: 这部电视剧播出后，主演一下子变得家喻户晓。
examples.en: After the series aired, its lead actor became a household name overnight.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive (家喻户晓的人物). Used of stories, people, brands. Positive or neutral.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，如"家喻户晓的人物"。用于故事、人物、品牌。

natural: Lifting a foot tips the balance

meaning.en: Pivotal; so important that every move one makes affects the outcome.
meaning.zh: 一抬脚就会影响两边的轻重。比喻所处地位重要，一举一动都关系到全局。

examples.zh: 中国在世界经济中占有举足轻重的地位。
examples.en: China holds a pivotal position in the world economy.

examples.zh: 他在公司里是个举足轻重的人物。
examples.en: He's a key figure in the company.

story.en: When Shu and Han were at war, an adviser told the general Dou Rong that the balance of power lay with him: "If you lift your foot to the left or right, you make one side heavier" (举足左右，便有轻重).
story.zh: 东汉初年，蜀、汉相争，有人对将军窦融说，胜负的关键在于他："举足左右，便有轻重。"

usage.en: Mainly attributive: 举足轻重的地位/作用/人物. Formal; news and writing.
usage.zh: 多作定语，如"举足轻重的地位/作用/人物"。书面语。

natural: No precedent in history

meaning.en: Unprecedented in history; never happened before.
meaning.zh: 历史上从来没有过的。

examples.zh: 这场洪水的规模史无前例。
examples.en: The scale of this flood is unprecedented.

examples.zh: 这次合作在两国关系中是史无前例的。
examples.en: This cooperation has no precedent in relations between the two countries.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. Formal and emphatic; stronger than 前所未有, implying a historical scale.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。书面语，语气比"前所未有"更重，强调历史规模。

natural: Heard so often one can recite the details

meaning.en: So familiar from hearing it often that one can repeat it in detail.
meaning.zh: 听得多了，能够详尽地说出来。

examples.zh: 这些童话故事孩子们都耳熟能详。
examples.en: The children know these fairy tales by heart.

examples.zh: 他唱的都是大家耳熟能详的老歌。
examples.en: He sang old songs everyone knows well.

story.en: Ouyang Xiu wrote that his mother often repeated his late father's sayings when teaching the family, so that "my ears grew familiar with them, and so I can tell them in detail" (吾耳熟焉，故能详也).
story.zh: 欧阳修在为父亲写的墓表中说，母亲平时教导子弟常用父亲的话，"吾耳熟焉，故能详也"。

usage.en: Predicate or attributive (耳熟能详的故事). The subject is the people who know it, or the thing known.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，如"耳熟能详的故事"。

natural: Rushing headlong into danger

meaning.en: To take desperate risks; to resort to reckless (often illegal) action out of desperation.
meaning.zh: 指在无路可走时采取冒险行动。

equivalents: desperate times call for desperate measures

examples.zh: 为了还赌债，他竟然铤而走险去抢劫。
examples.en: To pay off his gambling debts, he went as far as resorting to robbery.

examples.zh: 有些商家为了利润铤而走险，卖假货。
examples.en: Some sellers take reckless risks for profit by selling fakes.

story.en: A minister of Zheng wrote to Jin: a deer about to die doesn't pick a shady spot; a small state pushed too hard will "rush into danger — in desperation, how can it choose?" (铤而走险，急何能择).
story.zh: 郑国大夫写信给晋国，说鹿临死时顾不上选择好地方，小国被逼急了也会"铤而走险，急何能择"。

usage.en: Predicate. Negative; usually about crime or reckless decisions. 铤 is tǐng (not dìng).
usage.zh: 多作谓语，含贬义，多指犯罪或冒险行为。"铤"读 tǐng。

natural: Turning heaven and earth upside down

meaning.en: Earth-shaking; a complete and fundamental change.
meaning.zh: 形容变化巨大而彻底。

examples.zh: 改革开放以来，这座城市发生了翻天覆地的变化。
examples.en: Since the reforms, this city has been completely transformed.

examples.zh: 有了孩子以后，她的生活翻天覆地。
examples.en: After having a baby, her life was turned upside down.

usage.en: Most often in 翻天覆地的变化 (a dramatic transformation). Usually positive in news; can also describe chaos.
usage.zh: 最常见于"翻天覆地的变化"。新闻中多为褒义，也可形容闹得很厉害。

natural: Strike first to gain control of the other side

meaning.en: To strike first to gain the upper hand; to pre-empt.
meaning.zh: 先下手取得主动，制服对方。

examples.zh: 谈判一开始，对方就先发制人，提出了很高的要求。
examples.en: From the start of the negotiation, the other side struck first with high demands.

examples.zh: 这支球队喜欢先发制人，开场就猛攻。
examples.en: This team likes to seize the initiative and attack hard from kick-off.

story.en: When rebellion broke out against Qin, the governor of Kuaiji told Xiang Liang: "Strike first and you control others; strike later and you are controlled by them" (先发制人，后发制于人).
story.zh: 秦末各地起义，会稽郡守对项梁说："先发制人，后发制于人。"

usage.en: Predicate. Used in war, sport, business and arguments. Opposite: 后发制人 (wait and counter-attack).
usage.zh: 多作谓语，用于军事、体育、商业、辩论。相对的说法是"后发制人"。

natural: Going beyond what people expected

meaning.en: Unexpected; surprising.
meaning.zh: 超出人们的意料。

examples.zh: 比赛结果出人意料，冠军竟然是一名新人。
examples.en: The result was a surprise — the champion was a newcomer.

examples.zh: 出人意料的是，他主动辞职了。
examples.en: Unexpectedly, he resigned of his own accord.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; very common in the pattern 出人意料的是…… (surprisingly, …). Also 出乎意料.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，常说"出人意料的是……"。也说"出乎意料"。

natural: Shifting unseen and changing silently

meaning.en: To influence someone gradually and imperceptibly.
meaning.zh: 指人的思想、性格或习惯在不知不觉中受到感染、影响而发生变化。

examples.zh: 父母的言行对孩子有潜移默化的影响。
examples.en: Parents' words and actions have a subtle, gradual influence on their children.

examples.zh: 在中国住了几年，她的饮食习惯潜移默化地改变了。
examples.en: After a few years in China, her eating habits changed without her noticing.

origin.source: 北齐·颜之推《颜氏家训·慕贤》

story.en: Yan Zhitui advised his family to seek good company: when young, one is shaped by those around one without realising it — "changed in secret, transformed unseen, naturally becoming like them" (潜移暗化，自然似之).
story.zh: 颜之推告诫子孙要亲近贤人，因为人年少时会受周围人的熏陶，"潜移暗化，自然似之"。

usage.en: Usually attributive in 潜移默化的影响/作用, or adverbial. Neutral.
usage.zh: 多作定语"潜移默化的影响/作用"，也作状语。

natural: Not one mistake in ten thousand

meaning.en: Absolutely safe or certain; foolproof.
meaning.zh: 绝对不会出差错，非常稳妥。

examples.zh: 为了万无一失，他把文件又检查了一遍。
examples.en: To be absolutely sure, he checked the documents once more.

examples.zh: 这个计划并不是万无一失的。
examples.en: This plan isn't foolproof.

usage.en: Predicate, attributive or in 为了万无一失 (to be on the safe side). Often negated: 不是万无一失.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，常说"为了万无一失"，也常用否定"不是万无一失"。

natural: Looking on all with the same kindness

meaning.en: To treat everyone equally, without favouritism.
meaning.zh: 同样看待，不分厚薄。

examples.zh: 老师对所有学生都一视同仁。
examples.en: The teacher treats all her students equally.

examples.zh: 法律面前应该一视同仁。
examples.en: Everyone should be treated equally before the law.

story.en: Han Yu wrote that the sage "looks on all as one and treats them with equal kindness" (一视而同仁), caring for those near and far alike.
story.zh: 韩愈在《原人》中说："是故圣人一视而同仁，笃近而举远。"

usage.en: Predicate, often 对……一视同仁. In speech 一 is said yí (before 4th-tone 视).
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常说"对……一视同仁"。口语中"一"在第四声"视"前读 yí。

natural: Ending it by leaving it unfinished

meaning.en: To let a matter drop unresolved; to end without any proper conclusion.
meaning.zh: 该办的事情没有办完，放在一边不管，就算完事。

examples.zh: 大家提了很多意见，最后却不了了之。
examples.en: Lots of suggestions were made, but in the end nothing came of them.

examples.zh: 这件事不能就这样不了了之。
examples.en: We can't just let this drop without resolving it.

usage.en: Predicate; critical of matters (complaints, investigations, plans) that fizzle out. Both 了 are liǎo.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，批评事情没有结果就停了下来。两个"了"都读 liǎo。

natural: Carrying on the past and opening up the future

meaning.en: To carry on the legacy of the past and open up the way for the future.
meaning.zh: 继承前人的事业，开辟未来的道路。

equivalents: build on the past and look to the future

examples.zh: 新一代科学家肩负着继往开来的使命。
examples.en: The new generation of scientists carries the mission of building on the past and forging the future.

examples.zh: 这次大会是一次继往开来的会议。
examples.en: This congress marks a bridge between past achievements and future progress.

story.en: Zhu Xi praised Confucius for "continuing the sages of the past and opening learning for those to come" (继往圣，开来学).
story.zh: 朱熹称赞孔子"继往圣，开来学"，即继承古代圣人的学说，开启后人的学问。

usage.en: Formal; speeches, political documents and anniversaries. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 书面语，多见于讲话、政治文件、纪念场合。作谓语、定语。

natural: Mending the roof before it rains

meaning.en: To prepare in advance; to take precautions before trouble comes.
meaning.zh: 趁着天还没下雨，先修缮房屋门窗。比喻事先做好准备。

equivalents: fix the roof while the sun shines

examples.zh: 年轻时就要未雨绸缪，为养老做准备。
examples.en: Plan ahead while you're young and prepare for retirement.

examples.zh: 公司未雨绸缪，提前储备了原材料。
examples.en: The company took precautions and stocked up on raw materials in advance.

story.en: In this Book of Songs poem, a bird says: before the sky grows dark with rain, I gather mulberry roots to bind and mend my nest (迨天之未阴雨，彻彼桑土，绸缪牖户).
story.zh: 《诗经·鸱鸮》中一只鸟说："迨天之未阴雨，彻彼桑土，绸缪牖户。"意思是趁天还没下雨，剥取桑根把巢穴的门窗缠缚牢固。

usage.en: Predicate. Formal but common. Opposite of 临渴掘井 or 亡羊补牢 (acting after the fact). 缪 is móu here.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。较书面但常用。与"临渴掘井"相对。"缪"在这里读 móu。

natural: Binding him with the law

meaning.en: To bring someone to justice; to punish according to the law.
meaning.zh: 依据法律给以制裁。

equivalents: face the full force of the law

examples.zh: 这些贪官最终都被绳之以法。
examples.en: These corrupt officials were all eventually brought to justice.

examples.zh: 警方表示一定会将罪犯绳之以法。
examples.en: The police said they would bring the criminals to justice.

usage.en: Predicate, often passive (被绳之以法) or with 将/把 (将罪犯绳之以法). News and legal contexts.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用"被绳之以法""将……绳之以法"。用于新闻、法律。

natural: Prescribing medicine to suit the illness

meaning.en: To prescribe the right remedy; to tackle a problem according to its real cause.
meaning.zh: 针对病症用药。比喻针对具体问题采取有效措施。

equivalents: get to the root of the problem
tailor the solution to the problem

examples.zh: 要提高成绩，得先找出薄弱环节，再对症下药。
examples.en: To improve your grades, first find your weak points, then target them.

examples.zh: 政府针对就业难的问题对症下药，推出了一系列政策。
examples.en: The government tackled unemployment at its root with a series of targeted policies.

story.en: Two officials came to the famous doctor Hua Tuo with the same headache and fever. He gave one a purgative and the other a medicine to make him sweat. Asked why, he said one illness came from outside the body and the other from within, so they needed different treatment. Both recovered the next day.
story.zh: 两名官吏都头痛发热，去找名医华佗。华佗给一人开泻药，给另一人开发汗药。有人问为何不同，华佗说一个是外实，一个是内实，所以治法不同。第二天两人都痊愈了。

usage.en: Predicate. Used literally of medicine and, more often, of solving problems.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。可指医病，更多比喻解决问题。

natural: Already fine, yet seeking finer still

meaning.en: To constantly strive for perfection; to keep improving what is already good.
meaning.zh: 已经很好了，还要求更好。

examples.zh: 这位老师傅做家具精益求精，每个细节都不放过。
examples.en: The old carpenter strives for perfection, paying attention to every detail.

examples.zh: 我们要对产品质量精益求精。
examples.en: We must keep raising the standard of our products.

story.en: Commenting on the Book of Songs line "as if cut and filed, as if carved and polished", Zhu Xi explained that the craftsman, having made something fine, "seeks to make it finer still" (治之已精，而益求其精也).
story.zh: 朱熹解释《诗经》"如切如磋，如琢如磨"时说，工匠加工骨角玉石，"治之已精，而益求其精也"。

usage.en: Predicate; often 对……精益求精. Praises craftsmanship, quality and work attitude.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常说"对……精益求精"。用于赞扬工艺、质量和工作态度。

natural: Using up every last bit of strength

meaning.en: To do one's utmost; to spare no effort.
meaning.zh: 用尽全部力量。

examples.zh: 医生们竭尽全力抢救病人。
examples.en: The doctors did everything they could to save the patient.

examples.zh: 虽然输了，但我们已经竭尽全力了。
examples.en: We lost, but we gave it everything we had.

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial. Close to 全力以赴; 竭尽全力 stresses using up all one's strength, often in a struggle.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语。与"全力以赴"相近，更强调用尽力气。

natural: Not knowing whether to cry or laugh

meaning.en: Not knowing whether to laugh or cry; caught between amusement and exasperation.
meaning.zh: 哭也不好，笑也不好。形容处境尴尬，不知如何是好。

equivalents: not know whether to laugh or cry

examples.zh: 孩子把我的护照涂成了彩色，真让我哭笑不得。
examples.en: My kid coloured in my passport — I didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

examples.zh: 他这个解释让人哭笑不得。
examples.en: His explanation was so absurd it left everyone torn between laughing and despairing.

usage.en: Predicate, often 让/令人哭笑不得. Common in speech for absurd or awkward situations.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常说"让人哭笑不得"。口语常用，形容荒唐、尴尬。

natural: Not knowing where to put oneself

meaning.en: At a loss; not knowing what to do.
meaning.zh: 不知道怎样办才好。形容惊慌或为难。

equivalents: like a deer in the headlights

examples.zh: 突然被叫上台发言，她一时不知所措。
examples.en: Suddenly called up to speak, she was momentarily at a loss.

examples.zh: 面对这么多选择，我反而不知所措了。
examples.en: Faced with so many choices, I didn't know what to do.

story.en: The phrase appears in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, describing people so alarmed that they "did not know where to put themselves" — 措 meaning to place or arrange.
story.zh: 语出《三国志》，形容人惊惶得"不知所措"，"措"即安放、处置。

usage.en: Predicate, often with 一时 (for a moment). Also 手足无措 for the physical sense of being flustered.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与"一时"连用。另有"手足无措"。

natural: Coming back in a cloud of dust

meaning.en: To stage a comeback after a defeat; to return in force.
meaning.zh: 卷起尘土又回来了。比喻失败后重新恢复势力。

examples.zh: 去年输掉了决赛，今年他们卷土重来。
examples.en: They lost last year's final, and this year they're back for another shot.

examples.zh: 专家提醒，流感可能会在冬天卷土重来。
examples.en: Experts warn that flu may come back in force this winter.

story.en: Du Mu's poem on the spot where Xiang Yu killed himself after defeat imagines that, had he crossed the river home instead, the many talented young men there might have helped him "roll up the dust and come again" (卷土重来未可知).
story.zh: 杜牧在项羽兵败自刎的乌江亭题诗："江东子弟多才俊，卷土重来未可知。"惋惜项羽没有回江东重整旗鼓。

usage.en: Predicate. Positive of a person's comeback; negative of diseases, problems or enemies returning. 卷 is juǎn.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。用于人东山再起时偏褒义，用于疾病、问题时偏贬义。"卷"读 juǎn。

natural: Reason on one's side, spirit strong

meaning.en: Confident and bold because one believes one is in the right.
meaning.zh: 理由充分，所以说话做事有气势。

examples.zh: 我没做错事，所以可以理直气壮地说出真相。
examples.en: I did nothing wrong, so I can tell the truth with my head held high.

examples.zh: 他明明迟到了，还说得理直气壮。
examples.en: He was clearly late, yet he talked as if he were completely in the right.

usage.en: Adverbial (理直气壮地说) or predicate. Positive when justified; ironic when someone is shamelessly sure of themselves.
usage.zh: 多作状语，如"理直气壮地说"；也作谓语。有理时为褒义，用于讽刺时略带贬义。
